subject.title: Feature request: api.callGatewayMethod() for inter-plugin communication

question: Should ordinary third-party plugins be allowed to invoke Gateway methods registered by other plugins, and if so should the API be raw method dispatch, allowlisted request, or typed service/capability contracts?
rationale: The code already has trusted-only and HTTP-route-only dispatch paths, but expanding this to arbitrary plugin runtime code changes public SDK and security boundaries that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design an authorized SDK contract
options.body: Expose a narrow caller with explicit plugin eligibility, caller attribution, method exposure rules, docs, and contract tests.

options.title: Keep trusted-only Gateway requests
options.body: Document that ordinary third-party plugins should use existing runtime events, HTTP routes, or future service contracts instead of Gateway RPC dispatch.

options.title: Expose raw method dispatch
options.body: Allow plugins to call method strings directly and accept the broader compatibility and authorization surface as a product decision.

recommendation.title: Design an authorized SDK contract
recommendation.body: Expose a narrow caller with explicit plugin eligibility, caller attribution, method exposure rules, docs, and contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete landed the current constrained trusted Gateway seam and is the best available owner for deciding whether to broaden it.
